newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel aims for '97 double digit growth.
newsitem.headline: SingTel aims for '97 double digit growth.

text.p: Singapore Telecom chairman Koh Boon Hwee told reporters on Friday that the company aimed to maintain double digit growth next year.
"It is our goal to still try to maintain double digit profit growth in 1997," he said.
He was asked whether price cuts in international telephone calls would eat into the companies profits for next year.
He said a lot of the profit growth would depend upon the performance of the Singapore economy and there would be some pressure on margins.
Earlier SingTel annnounced that its first half net profit in the six months to September 30 rose 13.6 percent to Singapore $843.5 million on a turnover of S$2.17 billion.
Gautam Katoor regional telecommunications analyst for Dutch bank ING Barings said the results looked better than analysts were expecting.
"Operating cost controls were pretty good," he said.
The rise in traffic expenses was substantially lower than the 13 percent growth in IDD (International Direct Dialling) call volumes, Katoor added.
